title: Ukrainian ground robots and drones may have taken a Russian position with no infantry and no Ukrainian losses; the location, date, unit and prisoner count are undisclosed
summary: Zelenskyy (13 April 2026): an enemy position was taken “exclusively by unmanned platforms” with no infantry and no losses, per Politico and Business Insider; no location, date or verification.
account: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave an Arms Makers' Day address on Monday 13 April 2026. “For the first time in the history of this war, an enemy position was taken exclusively by unmanned platforms — ground systems and drones,” he said. He added that “the occupiers surrendered, and the operation was carried out without infantry and without losses on our side” (Politico, Business Insider, Censor.NET). He said ground robotic systems performed more than 22,000 missions on Ukraine's front line in the first three months of 2026. He named Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia. Newsweek says he did not say where the advance took place. No outlet gives a date, unit or prisoner count. Ars Technica says the claim is not independently verified and may refer to a 3rd Separate Assault Brigade action in Kharkiv Oblast last year. Politico calls the robots “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”.
purpose: Ukrainian unmanned ground vehicles and drones are built to carry out front-line missions in place of soldiers. Those missions include assaults, logistics and evacuation. Taking a position without exposing infantry is that purpose.
system: Ukrainian unmanned ground vehicles (Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia, as named by Zelenskyy) operating with aerial drones
developer: Ukrainian makers of the named systems (Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector, Volia)
domain: Defense: ground robotic systems in assault operations
segment: Unmanned ground vehicles and drones in combat
taxonomy_note: A combat action with no friendly losses is read as reduced potential for harm; no defense type exists.

ratings.reason: The capture, the surrender and the absence of losses rest solely on the President's statement. Newsweek says no location was given. Ars Technica and The Debrief say the claim is not independently verified, so the outcome is not established.

ai_role.statement: No source describes an AI function in this operation. Politico says the ground robotic systems are “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”. Jacob Parakilas of RAND Europe writes in The Conversation that they are “mostly still remotely operated”. He says autonomy is limited to tasks such as highlighting identified enemy positions. The Debrief says it is unclear how much remote human control was involved at each stage. Politico separately notes a January 2026 case in which a DevDroid robot “equipped with artificial intelligence elements” took three prisoners, a different event.

fields.account: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave an Arms Makers' Day address on Monday 13 April 2026. “For the first time in the history of this war, an enemy position was taken exclusively by unmanned platforms — ground systems and drones,” he said. He added that “the occupiers surrendered, and the operation was carried out without infantry and without losses on our side” (Politico, Business Insider, Censor.NET). He said ground robotic systems performed more than 22,000 missions on Ukraine's front line in the first three months of 2026. He named Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia. Newsweek says he did not say where the advance took place. No outlet gives a date, unit or prisoner count. Ars Technica says the claim is not independently verified and may refer to a 3rd Separate Assault Brigade action in Kharkiv Oblast last year. Politico calls the robots “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”.

fields.summary: Zelenskyy (13 April 2026): an enemy position was taken “exclusively by unmanned platforms” with no infantry and no losses, per Politico and Business Insider; no location, date or verification.
fields.account: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave an Arms Makers' Day address on Monday 13 April 2026. “For the first time in the history of this war, an enemy position was taken exclusively by unmanned platforms — ground systems and drones,” he said. He added that “the occupiers surrendered, and the operation was carried out without infantry and without losses on our side” (Politico, Business Insider, Censor.NET). He said ground robotic systems performed more than 22,000 missions on Ukraine's front line in the first three months of 2026. He named Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia. Newsweek says he did not say where the advance took place. No outlet gives a date, unit or prisoner count. Ars Technica says the claim is not independently verified and may refer to a 3rd Separate Assault Brigade action in Kharkiv Oblast last year. Politico calls the robots “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”.
